airhorn.d: The Airhorn is a weightless, mid-high value Scrap that can be found on almost every Moon. The horn itself is red and blue, with a yellow label for a fictional brand reading “AIRY BLAST”.

ammo.d: Ammo (short for 'ammunition'), a.k.a. Shotgun shell, is a consumable item in the game, exclusively dropped from Nutcrackers. It becomes available for collection after defeating a Nutcracker.

apparatus.d: Sell for ~80, or keep one for the Repress ship repair (needed for every ending). Pulling it cuts the building's power.

bell.d: The Bell (or "Brass bell") is a Scrap item in Lethal Company. It is considered common, appearing on more than half of the game's Moons and is mid-to-high tier in terms of value. It does not have any particular use or possible interactions.

belt bag.d: The Belt bag is a blue fanny pack that can be purchased from the equipment store for , used for carrying multiple equipment items with only a single hotbar slot taken up.

big bolt.d: The Big bolt is a low-value Scrap that's able to spawn on almost every moon. Despite its name, the Big bolt appears to be a screw, not a bolt. As it is made of metal, it can trigger a lightning strike during stormy weather.

binoculars.d: Binoculars are a scrapped equipment item. They can be spawned in with mods but are not functional. There is also a bug involving Gifts where they can contain an item they shouldn't, Binoculars being one of the possibilities.

body.d: A Body is the corpse of a deceased employee, effectively a ragdoll which has inherited their appearance.

bone.d: A weightless body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. The model of this item is reused from [https://store.steampowered.com/app/1717770/The_Upturned/ The Upturned], another game by Zeekerss.

cash register.d: The Cash Register is a Scrap item in Lethal Company. It is considered uncommon, appearing mostly with low chances of on most of the Moons where it spawns, despite there being seven. It is a high tier item in terms of Value, along with Gold bars or Zed Dogs and is the heaviest item in the game.

clipboard.d: The clipboard (a.k.a. Training manual a.k.a. Service manual) is a pedagogical item which generates in the ship and in the Company Cruiser. Both contain multiple pages of gameplay information, interspersed with worldbuilding. They have little use beyond that. The "Training manual" clipboard will always appear to the left of the brake lever upon creating or loading a save, even if moved, left in a Belt bag, or lost.

clown horn.d: Produces a honking sound when used that can be heard by other employees and (some) nearby wildlife. As it is made of metal, it can trigger lightning strikes when placed on the ground or held by an employee during stormy weather.

dust pan.d: The Dust pan is a Scrap item that can only found in Experimentation. Though it weighs nothing, dustpans are very low value, only higher than the lowest values in the game, i.e. metal sheets and whoopie cushions.

easter egg.d: The Easter egg is a small, colorful egg with 5 variants. It can be thrown with , and has a small chance to explode upon hitting the ground. The chances of an Easter egg exploding are the same regardless of whether it's been dropped, thrown, or placed inside of another object such as the Cupboard.

egg.d: thumb|right| A newly-hatched Sapsucker, moments before calling for its mother These are the eggs laid by a mother Sapsucker. Similar to the Circuit bees' nest, they sell for a good price, but come with danger. When an egg has been carried a certain distance from its nest, it will hatch after six seconds to reveal a baby Sapsucker.

egg beater.d: The Egg beater is a low-value Scrap that can be found on Tier 1 Moons as well as Adamance. As it is made of metal, it can trigger lightning strikes when held by an employee or placed on the ground during stormy weather.

extension ladder.d: The Extension Ladder can be used to reach otherwise difficult-to-reach or inaccessible locations. It weighs nothing, making it easy for employees to carry.

flashlight.d: Flashlight Flashlights are tools used to emit light in a conical shape in front of an employee, aiding exploration. Fully charged flashlights last for 140 seconds.

foot.d: Foot A weightless body part Scrap that appears on both Rend and Dine.

gift.d: The Gift is a Scrap item that can be opened to reveal a different, random scrap item inside. The dropped scrap item can be anything that's normally able to spawn on whichever moon the Gift was originally found. The item may be two-handed, despite the Gift being a one-handed scrap item.

gold bar.d: Gold bar The Gold bar is a high-value Scrap item. It is a very rare and heavy scrap item with the highest possible value of any item in the game. Despite its weight only being beaten by Cash registers, it is a one-handed item.

hairdryer.d: Noisemaker: makes a loud sound (10 uses on its battery) that players and sound-hunting enemies hear. Can lure Eyeless Dogs away, but also gives you away. Otherwise sell (~80).

hand.d: Hand A very low-value body part Scrap exclusive to Dine.

heart.d: A rare, high-value body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. Hearts will continuously make a beating sound, which allows them to be heard from a distance and located easier.

homemade flashbang.d: The Homemade Flashbang is similar to the Stun grenade, but its "fuse" is extremely short. Pulling the pin will cause it to explode almost immediately, flashing everything in the vicinity, but also dealing minor damage (20HP) to the employee that was holding it.

jetpack.d: The jetpack is a versatile yet clunky mobility tool used to travel around the surface of the moons. It is both the heaviest and most expensive piece of equipment in the game, but it makes up for this with its incredible aerial mobility. Its near-exclusively vertical thrust and incredible weight make it practically worthless within the interior areas of moons.

key.d: A small golden key. Used to unlock locked doors within interiors or the door to the Cabin on Adamance and is consumed on use. The key is made of metal and can trigger lightning strike on a stormy moon.

kitchen knife.d: The Kitchen Knife is a type of scrap that can also function as weapon for eliminating entities or destroying spider webs. It has a fixed sell value of .

knee.d: Knee The Knee is a body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. It's the only body part item aside from the Heart that weighs more than .

laser pointer.d: The Laser pointer is a mid-to-high-value Scrap that can be powered on like a Flashlight. When turned on, it emits a small orange light beam with an estimated range of 20m and 5 minutes of battery life. Impractical use for navigation, but it can be used as a replacement for Flashlights if you're out of options. The laser dot will be obscured by fog, steam, blizzards, and toxic fumes.

lockpicker.d: Lockpickers are tools used to gain access to locked doors. Upon placing one on a locked door, it remains there for 30 seconds before falling to the ground and unlocking the door. They are not consumed through use allowing them to be used repeatedly.

magic 7 ball.d: Magic 7 ball The Magic 7 ball is a mid-value Scrap. It's a play on the iconic toy series "Magic 8 Ball". Despite its name, it has no magical properties and cannot give answers to questions.

magnifying glass.d: Magnifying glass The Magnifying glass is a mid-value Scrap with translucent blue glass. Despite being an object you'd expect to hold up to your eye, this item is not inspectable in-game.

maneater.d: The Maneater is a deceptively cute indoor entity resembling an insect. While it initially appears to be a sensitive, carriable infant requiring constant care and maintenance, it transforms into a monstrous, extremely fast and deadly enemy if upset or provoked. The moon they are most commonly found on is Vow.

mapper.d: The Mapper (called Mapper tools in the store) is a utility item, which may eventually be purchasable but is currently inaccessible in-game. (A purchase flow exists, but it has the price of the Shovel and will add one of those to the Dropship instead.)

masks (item).d: Masks cannot possess an employee if the employee does not put it on themselves. Dying with a mask in one's inventory or holding it without putting it on does nothing.

mug.d: Mug The Mug (or, "Coffee mug") is a low-to-mid-value Scrap that can spawn in one of 5 different variants.

old phone.d: The Old phone is a mid-value Scrap depicting a black satellite phone. When switching to this item while it is in your inventory, it will play an audio clip: firstly a garbled static sound, followed by someone screaming, and finally a long disconnect tone. This sound can be heard by other players and hearable entities, such as Eyeless Dogs.

pro-flashlight.d: Though Pro-Flashlights only weigh 5 pounds, it is enough to noticeably affect running speed and stamina depletion. For example, when trying to secure Bee Hives, it is advised to leave these flashlights at the ship for an extra few seconds of running.

radar-booster.d: The Radar Booster can be purchased in the Store. When turned on, it can be used as another camera from the terminal. It also appears when an employee scans (right clicks).

remote.d: Turns lights on and off in ship when activated.

shotgun.d: The Shotgun is a scrap item that also functions as a weapon. It does not generate naturally, and is instead only wielded and dropped by Nutcrackers, along with however many shells the Nutcracker had in the shotgun when it died, with 2 extra shells dropped alongside it. It has a fixed sell value of regardless of how many shells are loaded.

shovel.d: The Shovel can be used to eliminate Entities or destroy Bunker Spider webs.

soccer ball.d: A generic-looking Soccer Ball, or football. Only Scrap Item in the game that can be moved without being picked up, as Players and other entities are able to kick it. It can still be held normally as a two-handed object. Will bounce off any entity it collides with, including entities most wouldn't expect, like Hygroderes, Circuit Bees and Roaming Locusts.

spray paint.d: Spray paint is a tool item that can be used to paint walls and floors, as well as other surfaces such as on-ship furniture items and even other employees. A can of spray paint must be shaken before it can be used- otherwise, the paint will dissipate into the air instead of being applied.

sticky note.d: The Sticky note is a pedagogical item which generates in the ship, hidden just to the left of the Terminal. Its sole purpose is to reveal the otherwise hidden command SIGURD, which is used to read unlocked Sigurd Logs.

stop sign.d: The Stop Sign is a scrap item that can be used to hit and damage certain entities, similarly to the Shovel and Yield sign. It is heavier than the Shovel but otherwise functionally identical.

stun grenade.d: Stun grenades are explosive weapons intended to disorient entities. tzp-inhalant.d: The TZP-Inhalant is a type of scrap that can be purchased from the store for credits. It temporarily increases an employee's speed, lowers the burden of their inventory weight, and reduces stamina drain when used by holding down left click. It can be used for 38 seconds before running out.

teeth.d: Teeth are a scrap item that continuously makes chattering noises when picked up. There is an 18% chance of disabling the noise when picked up. If dropped while chattering, it has a chance to move in a circular motion.

toothpaste.d: The Toothpaste item is an exclusive commodity found on the 5 most challenging moons within the game. Distinguished by its weightlessness, the Toothpaste item registers at on the scale. An interesting feature of this item is its atypical pricing range, fluctuating between and , a somewhat unusually broad spectrum in comparison to other items available.

toy robot.d: Robot toys are a scrap item that continuously makes loud toy noises when picked up. It can be picked up for a 25% chance of disabling the noise.

walkie-talkie.d: The Walkie-Talkie is used to communicate with co-workers beyond the proximity chat radius. It can transmit both voice and text (using the in-game chat) when activated.

whoopie cushion.d: Upon being walked over, the Whoopie Cushion emits a distinctive fart sound. It's essential to note that players are unable to activate the fart sound voluntarily when the item is held, it must be dropped and walked over. While the Whoopie Cushion may not yield significant value in terms of scrap, its appeal lies in its comedic value.

yield sign.d: A scrap item capable of hitting and damaging entities. Functions identically to the Stop Sign and Shovel items, but is significantly heavier than either of them, making it a less practical weapon.

zap gun.d: The Zap Gun is a type of scrap that can be purchased from the store for credits. It is a tool for stunning entities instead of directly damaging them.

zed dog.d: The Zed Dog is a plush fox that resembles ZedFox, the composer of the tracks "Boombox Song 5" and "Disco Ball" in Lethal Company.

mrov sauce.d: MorvDonalds' main scrap: about 101 credits each at 7 lb. The reason that moon is great money.

blank floppy disc.d: Craft on Galetry (2 Plastic stock, 1 Circuit boards, 3 Copper wiring). Insert into a moon's Floppy disc machine to make that moon's unlock disc (Selector, Dormant, Xenphir, Dune, Spine, Heap).

failsafe floppy disc.d: Under the right-hand counter of the Galetry gift shop (mod v7.0.0+). Translate it to re-unlock moons that vanished from your save.
